calibration.method: Each scored call (dated calls, COT calls, hypotheses, the weekly ledger forecast) is binned by its stated probability against how often it came true. One factor k scales every future call's distance from its own base rate: k is the Brier-optimal slope over the scored record, pulled toward 1 by a prior (0.3), clamped 0.25-1.5; it stays 1 until 30 calls are scored over 4+ weeks (pre-registered). In-sample Brier before / after is shown for transparency, not as proof. k cannot fix base rates that are themselves off: compare stated vs came true overall.

analogs.note: Descriptive, not a tested edge. Weekly fingerprints since 2007-01-19 (longer than the 2020+ window the owner's rule asks of trading backtests; 6 of the 20 analogs are 2020 or later). Each analog's features use data up to its own Friday; outcomes start at the first close after it (when that Friday's Treasury data were public). Analogs are at least 6 weeks apart and at least 13 weeks before now. Similarity = 1 / (1 + RMS distance of the z-scored features).

briefing.method: Insights are ranked by how unusual each reading is against its own history (z-scores of the 4-week changes), how close the scheduled release is, and how stretched positioning is. Hypothesis probabilities are the analogs' frequency of the same move, shrunk toward the frequency over all weeks (10 pseudo-cases), plus half the council tilt for gold, clamped 10-90%. Every hypothesis is recorded once a week in the calls ledger and scored on its date.
